blocks.text: A Scientist at DRDO, ISRO or CSIR conducts scientific research, develops technologies, performs experiments, analyses data and contributes to national research and development projects. This career path suits students interested in scientific discovery, engineering applications, laboratory research, space science, defence technology and advanced materials.

The Integrated BS-MS programme offered by institutions such as IISERs and NISER can provide a strong foundation for research careers. However, an integrated science degree does not automatically qualify a graduate for every scientist post. Eligibility depends on the specific recruitment notification, discipline, degree, experience and sometimes postgraduate or doctoral qualifications.
Research and laboratory science
Conduct experiments, test hypotheses, analyse findings and develop scientific methods or materials.
Space and defence research
Work on areas such as satellite systems, propulsion, sensors, materials, electronics, modelling and mission-related technologies, depending on qualifications and recruitment.

rows.text: Defence systems, materials, electronics, sensors, computing and applied sciences
Scientist recruitment has post-specific discipline and degree requirements.
Space science, satellites, launch vehicles, instrumentation and planetary research
Many technical Scientist/Engineer posts require specified engineering qualifications; science graduates should identify suitable science-research vacancies.
Research across physical sciences, chemicals, biology, materials, environment and related fields
Research institutes offer varied scientific, technical and project positions with different eligibility criteria.

blocks.text: An IISER or NISER degree is particularly relevant for research-oriented study. Students should check whether their intended post accepts an integrated BS-MS in the chosen subject rather than assuming all scientist recruitment routes are interchangeable.
Years 1–2
Build scientific foundations
Study core concepts in physics, chemistry, biology or mathematics. Strengthen calculus, statistics, laboratory methods, scientific writing and computational thinking.
Years 3–4
Choose a specialization
Take advanced subject courses, participate in laboratory or computational projects, learn research methods and seek supervised summer research internships.
Year 5
Complete advanced research
Undertake a dissertation or research project, present findings, obtain academic references and prepare applications for research posts or doctoral study.

IISERs offer five-year BS-MS programmes, while NISER offers a five-year Integrated MSc in basic sciences. Both are research-oriented pathways. Admission routes and eligibility are published through their official admissions systems.

rows.text: Space physics, optics, materials, sensors, instrumentation and computational physics
Advanced materials, chemical analysis, energetic materials and nanoscience
Biotechnology, molecular biology, microbiology, ecology and life sciences

blocks.text: The strongest choice is the subject you enjoy studying deeply and in which you can develop research expertise.
The Scientist role can be reached through several routes; the appropriate route depends on the employer and discipline.

rows.text: Relevant degree and any required examination, interview, experience or other conditions in the vacancy notice
Relevant postgraduate degree and selection under a specific fellowship advertisement
Qualification matching a funded research project's requirements
Advanced research training for roles that require doctoral expertise or specialized experience

blocks.text: For example, DRDO's Recruitment and Assessment Centre lists a first-class master's degree in relevant science subjects, mathematics or specified related disciplines among the essential qualifications for Scientist B science-category recruitment. Other conditions may apply to a particular advertisement.
RAC

ISRO publishes opportunities across scientific, engineering, technical and research categories. Its Scientist/Engineer vacancies can have specific degree and discipline requirements, so an integrated science degree should not be assumed to qualify for every engineering post.
ISRO
CSIR recruits scientists for its laboratories and institutes through its designated recruitment framework. Eligibility and selection procedures vary by scientist grade and vacancy.

Useful tools to learn

items.text: Python for scientific computing, data analysis and visualization.
MATLAB or GNU Octave for numerical modelling, where relevant.
R for statistical analysis, especially in biological and environmental research.
LaTeX for technical reports and research papers.
Discipline-specific laboratory, simulation or scientific-instrument software.

blocks.text: Students should seek supervised research opportunities at university laboratories, IISER and NISER research groups, national research institutes, and eligible DRDO, ISRO or CSIR laboratories.
Possible projects include:

blocks.label: Physics
blocks.text: Model the motion of an object under different forces or analyse optical measurements.

blocks.label: Chemistry
blocks.text: Compare material properties using approved laboratory methods and safety procedures.

blocks.label: Biology
blocks.text: Analyse a publicly available biological dataset or conduct a supervised ecological study.

blocks.label: Mathematics
blocks.text: Develop a numerical model for a real-world physical or environmental process.

blocks.label: Earth sciences
blocks.text: Analyse open satellite or climate datasets to study a geographic or environmental pattern.
For every project, document the research question, methodology, results, limitations and conclusions. Use original work and cite datasets and publications correctly.
Internship availability, selection criteria and funding differ across institutions and years. Check the official laboratory or organization website for current opportunities.
Depending on the intended role, investigate:

blocks.label: IISER Aptitude Test (IAT)
blocks.text: Admission route for eligible IISER programmes.

blocks.label: National Entrance Screening Test (NEST)
blocks.text: Admission route for the Integrated MSc programme at NISER and CEBS.

blocks.label: GATE
blocks.text: Relevant for certain recruitment routes and postgraduate opportunities; requirements vary by advertisement.

blocks.label: CSIR-UGC NET
blocks.text: Relevant to eligible postgraduate candidates pursuing specified research fellowships or academic pathways.

blocks.label: PhD entrance and fellowship selection
blocks.text: For research careers requiring doctoral training.

These examinations serve different purposes and are not universal requirements for all scientist jobs. Verify the latest eligibility, subject combinations and selection rules on the official websites.

items.text: Artificial intelligence for scientific discovery and simulation.
Space science, satellite data and planetary exploration.
Climate science, geospatial analysis and Earth observation.
Quantum science, optics and advanced instrumentation.

blocks.text: Students should develop strong fundamentals before specializing in emerging technologies.
Preparation progress
Select a core science specialization
Build strong subject knowledge and quantitative skills
Complete at least one supervised research project
Learn relevant scientific computing or laboratory tools
Prepare a research CV and project portfolio
Track official recruitment and fellowship notifications

blocks.label: Final recommendation
blocks.text: Students targeting scientist careers through IISER or NISER should focus on a strong science specialization, research experience, quantitative skills and scientific communication. Before choosing a degree or examination, compare its subject requirements with the current recruitment criteria of DRDO, ISRO or the relevant CSIR laboratory.
